w: Built 1093-1133 to replace an Anglo-Saxon church, the cathedral holds the shrines of St Cuthbert and the Venerable Bede. Its nave ceiling is the earliest surviving pointed rib vault anywhere. During the Wars of the Three Kingdoms, 3,000 captured Scottish soldiers were held inside; 1,700 died there.
s: Shrine of St Cuthbert and the earliest pointed rib vault
_facts: Contains the shrines of St Cuthbert and the Venerable Bede

Held 3,000 Scottish POWs during the Wars of the Three Kingdoms; 1,700 died there
Part of the Durham Castle and Cathedral World Heritage Site

w: Built between 1367 and 1390 by John Neville, 3rd Baron Neville de Raby, this castle was the birthplace of Cecily Neville, mother of the kings Edward IV and Richard III. Seized by the Crown after the failed 1569 Rising of the North, it remains the private seat of the Barons Barnard.
s: Birthplace of a Plantagenet king's mother

w: A ruined medieval castle in the County Durham town that shares its name. Little of the original fortress survives above ground today, but the remains still stand at the heart of the town that grew up around them.
s: The ruin that gave a town its name
_facts: Ruined medieval castle
Stands in the town of Barnard Castle, County Durham

n: Ushaw Historic House, Chapels and Gardens
w: Founded in 1808 by English Catholic scholars fleeing revolutionary France, Ushaw trained priests for the north of England and was a licensed Durham University hall until 2011. Its Georgian and Victorian Gothic chapels closed as a seminary, then reopened in 2014 as a heritage site now drawing over 100,000 visitors a year.
s: A refugee seminary turned Gothic chapel heritage site
_facts: Founded 1808 by scholars who fled France after the Revolution
Principal Catholic seminary for training priests in the north of England
Affiliated with Durham University from 1968 until closing in 2011
Reopened as a visitor attraction in 2014; over 100,000 visitors a year by 2023

w: One of only four complete Anglo-Saxon churches left standing in England, alongside those at Bradford-on-Avon, Greensted and Brixworth. This Grade I listed parish church, about a mile and a half from Bishop Auckland, has stood since the Saxon era.
s: One of four complete Anglo-Saxon churches surviving

w: The ruined piers of a Roman bridge span an old course of the River Tees between Piercebridge, County Durham, and Cliffe in North Yorkshire. Channel 4's Time Team excavated the site in 2009, exposing the foundations of the crossing that once carried Roman road traffic over the river.
s: Roman bridge piers dug up by Time Team in 2009
_facts: Ruin of a Roman bridge over the River Tees
